questions.questionText: A sum amounts to ₹7,562 in 4 years and to ₹8,469.44 in 5 years, at a certain rate percent per annum when the interest is compounded yearly. If ₹10,000 at the same rate of interest is borrowed for two years, then what will be the compound interest (in ₹)?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (A).

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - IX: PRINCIPAL BECOMES N TIMES AFTER T YEARS
questions.questionText: A sum of money at compound interest doubles itself in 4 years. In how many years does the sum become 8 times of itself at the same rate of interest?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (B).

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - IX: PRINCIPAL BECOMES N TIMES AFTER T YEARS
questions.questionText: A certain amount of money becomes thrice in 5 years at compound interest. How many years it will take to become 9 times?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (C).

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - IX: PRINCIPAL BECOMES N TIMES AFTER T YEARS
questions.questionText: Money is doubled in a bank account in 7 years, when the interest is compounded annually. What time in years is needed to make an amount 8 times in the bank?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (C).

questions.questionText: A sum of ₹4,000 is lent at 10% p.a., interest compounded annually. What is the difference between the compound interest for the 2nd year and the 3rd year?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (A).

questions.questionText: Mukesh invested ₹100000 in a company. He would be paid interest at 7% per annum compounded annually. Find the interest for the 3rd year.
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (D).

questions.questionText: A sum of money becomes two times of itself in 8 years at simple interest, and it becomes four times of itself in 2 years at compound interest, when interest is compounded annually. Find the ratio of the rate of simple interest to the rate of compound interest offered per year.
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (D).

questions.questionText: The difference between the compound interests on a certain sum for $1\frac{1}{2}$ years at a rate of 20% p.a. is ₹1,716 when the interest is compounded half yearly and compounded annually. The sum (in ₹) is:
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (D).

questions.questionText: A sum of ₹1,00,000 was taken from a bank at the rate of 7% p.a. to be compounded annually for 5 years. Calculate the compound interest. (Closest to a ₹)
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (D).

questions.questionText: Find the amount of ₹75,000 for one year at the rate of 16% per annum, if the interest is compounded quarterly (rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (C).

questions.questionText: If 10 percent per annum rate of compound interest compounded yearly is equivalent to the x percent per annum rate of compound interest compounded half yearly, then what is the value (Approximate) of x?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (C).

questions.questionText: A man invested a total of ₹12,050 in two parts, one at 10% p.a. simple interest for 2 years and the other at the same rate at compound interest, interest being compounded annually, for the same time. The amount he received from both the parts are equal. The sum (in ₹) invested at the compound interest is:
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionText: A and B together borrowed a sum of ₹51,750 at an interest rate of 7% p.a. compound interest in such a way that to settle the loan, A paid as much amount after three years as paid by B after 4 years from the day of borrowing. The sum (in ₹) borrowed by A was :
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (D).

questions.questionText: The compound interest on a sum of ₹12,000 at a rate of x % p.a. for $1\frac{1}{2}$ years is ₹3,840, compounded yearly. What will be the compound interest on the same sum at the same rate and for the same period if the interest is compounded half-yearly?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (A).

questions.questionText: Joseph deposited a total of ₹52,500 in a bank in the names of his two daughters aged 15 years and 16 years in such a way that they would get equal amounts when they become 18 years old. If the bank gives 10% compound interest compounded annually, then what is the amount (in ₹) that Joseph had deposited in the name of his younger daughter ?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (D).

questions.questionText: Divide ₹66,300 between A and B in such a way that the amount that A receives after 8 years is equal to the amount that B receives after 10 years; with compound interest being compounded annually at a rate of 10% per annum.
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionText: Nidhi invested her savings in schemes A and B in the ratio 2 : 3, respectively, for $1\frac{1}{2}$ years. Scheme A offers interest at 20% p.a. compounded half yearly, while Scheme B offers interest at 10% p.a. compounded yearly. If the total interest received by her from both the schemes is ₹13,524, then the amount (in ₹) invested by her in Scheme A is:
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionText: A certain sum was invested for three years in a scheme in which the interest gets compounded annually. During the first two years, the scheme provided growths at the rates of 80% and 60%, respectively, but during the third year there was a decline by 40%. What was the overall interest rate for three years?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (C).

questions.questionText: Loan is to be repaid in two equal yearly installments. If the rate of interest is 10% per annum, compounded annually, and each installment is ₹6,897, then find the total interest charged.
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionText: A loan of ₹2,550 is to be paid back in two equal half-yearly installments. How much is each installment if the interest is compounded half-yearly at 8% p.a.?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionText: An item is bought on a condition that three equal installments of ₹3,993 are to be paid at a rate of 10% compound interest, compounded annually. The cost of the item is:
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (D).

questions.questionText: A loan of ₹8,925 is to be paid back in two equal half-yearly installments. How much is each installment if the interest is compounded half-yearly at 8% per annum?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionText: A loan is to be returned in two equal yearly installments. If the rate of interest is 10% p.a., compounded annually and each installment is ₹6534, then the total interest charged (in ₹) is:
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (A).

questions.questionText: A certain loan was returned in two equal half yearly installments each of ₹6,760. If the rate of interest was 8% p.a., compounded yearly, how much was the interest paid on the loan?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (D).

questions.questionText: A loan is to be returned in two equal yearly installments. If the rate of interest is 10% p.a. compounded annually and each installment is ₹5,808 then 60% of the total interest (nearest to a ₹) charged in this scheme is:
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (D).

questions.questionText: Surekha borrowed a sum of money and returned it in two equal annual installments of ₹ 5547 each. If the rate of interest was $7\frac{1}{2}\%$ p.a. compounded yearly, then the total interest paid by her was :
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionText: A sum of ₹6,000 is to be paid back in two equal annual installments. Each installment is to be paid at the end of every year. How much is each installment if the interest is compounded annually at 2% p.a.? (Rounded off up to two decimal places)
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionText: Sita takes a loan of ₹35,000 at an interest rate of 10% compound interest, compounded annually. She agrees to pay two equal installments in 2 years, one installment at the end of each year. Find the value of each installment. (Round off to the nearest integer)
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (A).

questions.questionText: Rajnish borrowed ₹1,500 from a bank and repaid the entire amount with interest in two equal annual installments, the first installment being paid one year after Rajnish borrowed from the bank. If the rate of interest was 40% per annum, compounded annually, then what was the value (in ₹) of each installment paid by Rajnish?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (C).

questions.questionText: A mobile phone is available for ₹79,860 by cash payment or by paying cash of ₹60,000 as down payment and the remaining amount in three equal annual installments. If the shopkeeper charges interest at the rate of 10% per annum compounded annually, then the amount of each installment (in ₹) will be:
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionText: A money lender finds that due to the fall in the annual rate of interest from 18% to 15%, his yearly income diminishes by ₹750. His capital is:
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionText: Geeta deposited a certain sum of money in her bank account which amounted to ₹27,783 in 3 years at 5% per annum, the interest being compounded annually. What amount did she deposit?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionText: A man borrowed ₹50,000 from a bank at 10% per annum, compounded annually. At the end of every year, he pays ₹15,000 as part payment of the loan and interest. How much does he still owe to the bank after three such installments?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (A).

questions.questionText: Amit borrows a sum of ₹8,000 at 10% p.a. compound interest for 4 years. He repays ₹2,800 at the end of the first year and ₹2,600 at the end of the second year. To clear the loan, how much should he pay after 4 years, interest being compounded yearly?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (C).

questions.questionText: A man borrowed a certain sum and agrees to repay it by paying ₹4000 at the end of first year and ₹7700 at the end of second year. If the rate of compound interest compounded annually is 10% per annum, then find the sum (in ₹)
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (D).

questions.questionText: A person borrowed a sum of ₹30800 at 10% p.a. for 3 years, interest compounded annually. At the end of two years, he paid a sum of ₹13268. At the end of 3rd year, he paid ₹x to clear of the debt. What is the value of x?
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (C).

questions.questionText: A certain sum is deposited for 4 years at a rate of 10% per annum on compound interest compounded annually. The difference between the interest at the end of 2 years and that at the end of 4 years is ₹5082. Find the sum (in ₹)
questions.solution: According to the official TCS answer key, the correct option is (A).
